title: Structured output error-mode matrix and E2E verification
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: PRD-fragment: Define unambiguous acceptance criteria, verification tests, and operational telemetry for structured outputs with streaming and function/tool calling. Focus is on enumerating error modes (schema mismatch, truncated stream, tool failure, partial object emission, duplicate/tool reentry), mapping each to deterministic platform behavior and fallbacks, and specifying E2E tests that validate behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Error-mode matrix documented and approved by PM+Eng+Design. Each mode lists expected platform actions, HTTP/stream status codes, and whether payload is persisted for replay.

AC-2: For 'schema-mismatch' during streaming, system emits a typed FRAME with status=validation_error, includes byte_offset, and closes the stream with canonical error envelope unless a soft-fallback policy is configured.

AC-3: For 'truncated_stream' (partial object at EOF), runtime must persist last checkpoint token in call metadata and surface a resumable_token in final envelope when model indicates continuation possible.

AC-4: For 'tool_failure' during function call, API returns structured tool_error frame containing tool_id, failure_class (retryable|non-retryable), and suggested mitigation (fallback_model|noop|retry-after).

AC-5: For 'partial_object' emissions (object fields streamed across frames), the client-visible API must never expose an object until object-level commit frame is emitted; intermediate frames are trace-only and accessible via debug-level trace logs only.

AC-6: Idempotency: repeated function-calls with identical idempotency_key must result in at-most-once tool invocation; platform records invocation_id and surface invocation_id in telemetry and final envelope.

AC-7: Streaming fallback policy: when latency SLO at edge is violated mid-stream, runtime triggers a 'fast-fallback' to a smaller model and emits a fallback_frame that explains reduction (model_id, reason, estimated_quality_impact).

AC-8: Observability: each acceptance test must produce telemetry events (emission_phase, frame_status, schema_validation, tool_outcome) with sample rate >= 100% in internal staging and >= 1% in canary production, and those keys must be visible in the Console exploratory view.

AC-9: Security: structured frames may include sensitive metadata only when KMS is enabled for the tenant; tests must validate that private deployments without KMS do not leak plaintext secrets in frames.
AC-10: Backwards compatibility: existing non-streaming clients continue to receive final JSON envelopes unchanged for calls with stream=false.
success_metrics: SM-1: Schema validation errors in production < 0.05% of structured-output calls within 30 days of rollout
SM-2: Resumable stream recovery success rate >= 98% in staging under injected 5% truncated_stream fault injection
SM-3: Tool duplicate-invocation incidents = 0 for calls with idempotency_key set across 30 days
SM-4: Mean time to detect (MTTD) frame-level validation errors < 5 minutes after rollout via Console alerts
testing_plan: Unit: schema validator tests for positive and negative examples (strict & permissive modes).
Integration: function-calling harness that simulates tool latency, transient errors, and explicit non-retryable failures. Validate tool_error frames and idempotency_id recording.

E2E-canary: Deploy to a single region on hosted with 2% traffic. Run canary suite that includes: TC-001 truncated_fragment_resume, TC-002 partial_object_commit_order, TC-003 fallback_model_switch_midstream, TC-004 idempotent_tool_duplicate_suppression.
Fault-injection: Inject 'truncated_stream' and 'tool_timeout' at runtime and assert recovery behavior according to error-mode matrix. Use chaos-monkey job that runs daily against staging for 72h.
Interoperability: Validate non-streaming SDKs (Python/JS/Go) receive consistent final envelopes when stream=false; streaming SDKs must support incremental on_commit callbacks and resume APIs.
Security tests: Run static scans and dynamic tests to ensure frames containing secrets are encrypted when KMS enabled; run privacy audit on stored checkpoints.
test_cases: TC-001: truncated_fragment_resume - Start a streaming structured response, force EOF while last object missing closing field. Expect resumable_token in final envelope and successful resume that completes object when resumed with token.
TC-002: partial_object_commit_order - Emit object fields out-of-order across frames, ensure no object is exposed before commit frame and final object matches canonical schema on commit.

TC-003: tool_nonretryable - Function call returns non-retryable error. Expect tool_error frame with failure_class=non-retryable, no auto-retry, and consumer-visible final_envelope with error_code and mitigation hint.

TC-004: fast_fallback_midstream - Inject increased model latency to breach SLO after stream start. Expect fallback_frame with fallback_model and quality_impact estimate, and stream continues under fallback model.
TC-005: duplicate_tool_invoke - Replay same idempotency_key twice from client. Ensure platform invokes tool at most once and returns same invocation_id in both responses.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): library-level validators enabled, local harness passes.
Phase 1 (staging): Enable full telemetry and fault-injection. Run 72h chaos tests.

Phase 2 (canary): Deploy to hosted region us-west-2 at 2% traffic, enable schema-strict for 50% of canary traffic and permissive for the rest, monitor Console dashboards and rollback on threshold breach.

Phase 3 (gradual): Ramp to 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 7 days with monitoring gates at each step. Dedicated customers will be contacted 10 business days before final switch; Private installs will receive an opt-in upgrade bundle.
open_tradeoffs: Tradeoff A: strict schema validation reduces downstream parsing errors but increases false positives for heuristically-correct model outputs. Mitigation: support tenant-level permissive mode for first 30 days.
Tradeoff B: storing resumable checkpoints increases reliability but raises storage costs and retention questions. Mitigation: default 7-day TTL and opt-in longer retention for enterprise customers.
Tradeoff C: fallback to smaller model reduces latency but may degrade output quality. Mitigation: expose quality_impact estimate and allow caller policy to opt-out.
